stories.headline: Max Verstappen admits to McLaren, Mercedes talks before 'following heart' with Red Bull stay
stories.summary: Max Verstappen has admitted to serious talks with McLaren and Mercedes before agreeing his Red Bull extension last month.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen has admitted to serious talks with McLaren and Mercedes before agreeing his Red Bull extension last month.

Verstappen ended a long period of uncertainty about his future with the new Red Bull deal, announced ahead of his home race, the Dutch Grand Prix, which overwrote a deal lasting until 2028 with one running through to the end of 2030.

The existence of escape clauses in his old deal had allowed rumours of moves elsewhere to spread.

Verstappen has acknowledged that he explored options with rival teams before committing to a longer deal.

"Of course, any kind of chat you take seriously," Verstappen said in a BBC Sport interview when asked about how serious talks were with McLaren and Mercedes. "They're all very respectful chats. There's nothing wrong with that."

Verstappen has been with Red Bull for his entire Formula 1 career. The company signed him to a developmental deal in 2014 before handing him a debut with junior team Toro Rosso the following season.

He memorably won for Red Bull on his first appearance with the team after replacing Daniil Kvyat at the 2016 Spanish Grand Prix.

He spent five seasons at the team before winning his first championship in 2021, the first of four consecutive titles.

- Spanish Grand Prix: Everything you need to know about the Madring

- Red Bull sign Kimi Raikkonen's son Robin, 11

- Leclerc advice for Max vs. 100 drivers: Don't crash!

Verstappen pointed out he could have left Red Bull in those fallow years and ultimately opted to stay this time around as he believes Red Bull can be contenders again in future.

"I felt that staying was, for me, the right choice," he said. "You have to follow your heart. I could have run away very early on in my Red Bull career and gone somewhere else to try and win. If you have a little bit of patience, you do end up winning. I feel like that's my approach now as well."

Part of the uncertainty around Verstappen's future had been linked to his discontent with Formula 1's controversial new hybrid engines, which have shifted a lot of emphasis onto energy management and deployment.

Verstappen has labelled this "anti-racing" and likened the new F1 to Mario Kart.

F1 is making tweaks to the engines in 2027 and 2028 to lessen the importance of the electrical elements and Verstappen hopes this will lead to an improvement in how the racing feels.

"Hoping that it will be better in the future," he said. "Accepting where we are at the moment. Still the love for the sport. Not at the moment the driving. But the love for the sport.

"I love competition, naturally. I just hope that in the coming years, towards 2030, it can only get better. And to start to make the best of it, because these are the rules for the next four or five years."

stories.headline: Arena for 76ers, Flyers to open in 2030, marks 'new era'
stories.summary: The 76ers and Flyers have unveiled renderings of their new fully privately funded arena in South Philadelphia, which is targeted to open before the WNBA season in 2030.
stories.body:
The 76ers and Flyers have unveiled renderings of their new arena on the former Spectrum site in South Philadelphia, which the organizations are calling the largest fully privately funded project in city history.

The arena is now targeted to open before the WNBA season in 2030, when Philadelphia's expansion team will begin play. The Sixers, owned by Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment (HBSE), come in as 50-50 partners with Comcast Spectacor in the new arena, after spending more than a decade as tenants.

"This is a new era for Philadelphia sports," Comcast chairman Brian Roberts said. "To build our future where Ed Snider and the Spectrum made history makes this project truly special. Working with HBSE, we are creating a world-class experience worthy of Philadelphia's incredible fans."

The Spectrum-inspired design includes more than a half-acre of outdoor gathering space, with fan plazas, food and beverage options and a large entrance staircase inspired by the steps at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

"Philly fans deserve the best arena in the world, and we are excited to partner with Comcast to deliver just that," Sixers managing partner Josh Harris said. "This privately funded arena will be the home to moments and memories that define this city for generations."

Added NBA commissioner Adam Silver: "I'm thrilled to see the first renderings of what promises to be an extraordinary home for NBA and WNBA basketball as well as many other world-class events. Beyond the incredible experience the new arena will bring to fans, I commend HBSE and Comcast for such a significant economic investment in Philadelphia."

For the Flyers, the move brings the franchise back to the grounds where it began play in 1967 and won its only two Stanley Cups.

Since taking over as Flyers governor in 2023, Dan Hilferty has also overseen a restructuring of Philadelphia's front office and made returning the franchise to consistent Stanley Cup contention a priority.

"This new arena will be a state-of-the-art home worthy of the Flyers, their fans, and the entire city," NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said. "Comcast Spectacor and HBSE's commitment to this project reflects a shared belief in Philadelphia's future and a lasting investment in the city's economic vitality."

The organizations project the arena will create nearly 15,000 jobs and generate nearly $6 billion in economic activity over the next decade, along with hundreds of millions of dollars in new tax revenue benefiting the city and the School District of Philadelphia.

stories.headline: Germany beats South Korea, rolls into World Cup quarterfinals
stories.summary: Host Germany advanced to the quarterfinals of the women's FIBA World Cup with a morale-boosting 94-56 rout of South Korea on Tuesday, and the United States learned its next opponent.
stories.body:
BERLIN -- Host Germany advanced to the quarterfinals of the women's FIBA World Cup with a morale-boosting 94-56 rout of South Korea on Tuesday, and the United States learned its next opponent.

Hungary, which beat Japan 84-63, will play the four-time defending champion U.S. on Thursday.

Germany captain Marie Gülich led her team to a quarterfinal against European champion Belgium with 19 points and five rebounds.

Every German score elicited huge cheers from the appreciative home fans at the Berlin Arena, particularly in the first half. Germany led by 17 points at halftime.

The home team has been gradually improving since losing its first group game by 30 points to Spain. Germany rebounded with a 74-58 win over Japan and followed with an 83-58 win over Mali.

Hungary eliminates Japan Réka Lelik led Hungary with 23 points and eight rebounds in a surprisingly comfortable win over Japan earlier.

Virág Takács-Kiss also had eight rebounds and added 17 points for Hungary, which will face the U.S. in the late quarterfinal slot Thursday.

"It feels incredible. It's been 40 years since we went to the quarterfinals and I still can't believe it," Lelik said.

The game was overshadowed by a serious injury to Japan shooting guard Saki Hayashi, who went off with what looked a broken right arm after an awkward fall.

Hayashi needed immediate medical attention a foul in the air from Agnes Torok with just over a minute left in the second quarter. A blue tarp was provided to give her privacy and fans responded with applause when she was led off.

Japan connected on only seven 3-pointers Tuesday. The Japanese had set a record with 20 three-pointers in a World Cup game on Friday before France broke it with 22 on Monday.

Ramu Tokashiki's two free throws drew Japan level at 34-34, but that was as close as it got. Agnes Studer responded with a 3-pointer to give Hungary a 37-34 lead at halftime.

"They hit their open shots, we missed our open shots," Japan coach Corey Gaines said.

Hungary finished 11 of 25 from beyond the arc on the first of two days off for the U.S., which qualified directly for the quarterfinals as a group winner.

"I'm excited to play the very best players in the world, the best team in the word," Lelik said of Thursday's game. "I never got the opportunity to play against them. So I'm just very excited how it's going to be. And we're going to do everything for sure. But besides that, I want us to enjoy the game."

Still two places up for grabs All the quarterfinals are scheduled for Thursday. Spain and France await the winners of Wednesday's playoffs between Italy-Australia and China-Puerto Rico, respectively.

stories.headline: Jude Bellingham takes responsibility for Real Madrid not thrashing Inter Milan: 'Two sitters'
stories.summary: Jude Bellingham admitted he missed "two sitters" as Real Madrid struggled to a 2-1 Champions League win over Inter Milan at the Bernabéu.
stories.body:
Jude Bellingham admitted he missed "two sitters" as Real Madrid struggled to a 2-1 Champions League win over Inter Milan at the Bernabéu.

Visitors Inter were the better team for much of Tuesday's game, having more possession and creating more chances, but Madrid came out on top thanks to first-half goals from Kylian Mbappé and Federico Valverde.

Midfielder Bellingham was close to grabbing a third goal before halftime, and could have added another after the break -- set up by a spectacular dribble from Brahim Díaz -- as Inter pulled a goal back through Carlos Augusto to ensure a nervous finale.

"We created so many chances again tonight, myself included, two sitters," Bellingham told CBS. "The goalkeeper [Josep Martínez] has done well to be fair, but I've just got to put the ball in the net.

"The first one was just more instinct. The second one, I just got in my own head ... It's frustrating, not so much personally, but we could have made the game easier for the team.

"In the end we're defending a one-goal lead, backs to the wall, and people will probably forget all the good things we did, because we didn't win four or five nil, and that's partly my fault."

Bellingham has been one of the standout performers for Madrid so far this season under new coach José Mourinho, with two goals and two assists in LaLiga.

- Henry backs Mbappé for Ballon, Olise over Kane

- Mourinho: Trent isn't a midfielder despite CL start

- Giggs: Utd scouted Mbappé, didn't try to sign him

The team slipped to a 1-0 defeat at Real Betis on Friday to drop their first points of the season, but returned to winning ways against Inter, with Thibaut Courtois starring in goal.

"It could have finished five or six-one to us, or it could have finished 6-6," Mourinho said. "I wouldn't say [Inter] could have won, because we created more in the crucial moments, like the 3-0 for Jude at the end of the first half.

"It was a crazy game. I don't like that kind of madness, I like being able to score five or six or seven, but having absolute control, and not needing an incredible goalkeeper."

stories.headline: Under pressure: those with the biggest questions to answer in the semis
stories.summary: Two cut-throat AFL semifinals. Two of four teams facing the end of the road. And that means a host of individuals, players and coaches are under pressure. Rohan Connolly looks at who has the biggest questions to answer.
stories.body:
Two cut-throat AFL semifinals. Two of four teams facing the end of the road. That's the equation. And that means a host of individuals, players, and coaches are ... under pressure (yep, that Queen/David Bowie classic's going through my head now, too).

Go on, put it on and click your fingers to that bassline while you read about those most under the pump on Friday and Saturday evening.

Justin Longmuir
You won't find too many better recent examples of one result so starkly changing the narrative surrounding an AFL coach than Fremantle's loss to Hawthorn last Thursday night. Longmuir and his team had done everything right this season until then. Yet the bottom line remains they now teeter on the edge of a straight sets exit at home with Longmuir copping plenty of critical flak. The Dockers' ball movement was stymied, they were inefficient, with 57 forward entries producing only five goals, and Hawthorn created space far too easily. The "lack of flexibility" accusation has also popped up again, along with more talk about costly poor starts. Fremantle lost a home final last year to Gold Coast. A third home finals defeat in a row could damage Longmuir's reputational stocks irreparably.

Jeremy Cameron
There may not be another player under as much pressure to perform on Friday night as the dual Coleman medallist, who has been goalless for a month, and five times in his last seven outings. Cameron took just one mark and had only nine disposals against Carlton last week, lacked any sort of physical presence, and was drifting up around the wing to pick up what few touches he could manage. Cameron managed two goals in Geelong's narrow Round 15 loss to Fremantle in Perth, but even then the Cats were held to the second-lowest score of their last 10 outings. Anything less this week, and there will be an awful lot of responsibility upon the likes of Shannon Neale and Patrick Dangerfield to find Cameron's missing goals.

Josh Treacy
What's that expression, one day a rooster the next a feather duster? On August 25, Fremantle's Josh Treacy was being feted as the All-Australian centre half-forward for 2026. Just over a week later, he was getting towelled up by the critics for being "destroyed" by Hawthorn key defender Josh Battle. Treacy had just four disposals, no marks and kicked just one late consolation goal. He hadn't had a kick until late in the last quarter and was accused of not attacking the contest with his usual physical presence. It doesn't get any easier this week for him, either, given that last time Fremantle met Geelong, Connor O'Sullivan held him to 2.2 from only nine disposals, picking up 16 himself, six intercept marks and a coaches' vote. Treacy needs to improve on that effort and last week's significantly.

Patrick Dangerfield
Hang on. How can the best player on the ground in last week's elimination final be under pressure the very next game he plays? Well, being the long-time acknowledged champion he is, the Brownlow medallist is always under the microscope to an extent. If "Danger" plays a blinder, Geelong will generally win. That's pressure of its own. But then there's the memory of last year. Prior to last Friday night, it was in the 2025 preliminary final against Hawthorn that Dangerfield delivered his best September performance with 31 disposals and three goals. And the following week? Unfortunately, his banged-up 35-year-old frame couldn't repeat the dose, delivering a strangely muted 10-disposal effort in the grand final loss to Brisbane. Now, 12 months older, can he back up one superlative September effort with another?

Murphy Reid
Last year's Rising Star and this year's All-Australian might be a bit of a soft target given what he's done in two seasons, that he's only recently turned 20 and last week played only his second AFL final, but Reid was one of the biggest disappointments in Fremantle's soft qualifying final performance. Whether missing the two games prior with a groin niggle has thrown him out of his stride is an interesting question, but his usually precise kicking was unusually off-target against the Hawks, and his off night was a major factor in Fremantle lacking so much of the spark the headbanded youngster has brought to the team and which had typified their season to date.

Lachie Neale
The dual Brownlow medallist was hardly the only Lion to have a poor one last week, but there's several reasons he's probably under more pressure than nearly all his teammates this week. Most obviously, given the widespread expectation that he's headed elsewhere in 2027, this could well be his final game for the club. Plus he and the other midfielders are coming off a pantsing by the Swans and, in Neale's case, Jai Serong. Even if the Lions are to get through this, Neale remains under pressure; Brisbane would face the all-conquering Hawks, before potentially the Swans again or an old September foe in Geelong, with tagger Oisin Mullin looming as another handbrake on the two-time Brownlow winner. Neale's record in finals overall is stellar, but Brisbane has seldom needed one of his best September performances more.

Matthew Nicks
OK, let's be clear, Nicks isn't going to lose his job if Adelaide can't pull an upset against Brisbane at the Gabba, even though he might have had the Crows not beaten the Bulldogs last week. But pressure? That hasn't suddenly evaporated just because a rested Adelaide beat a lesser-ranked opponent at home and gave Nicks his first finals win. The stigma of last year's straight sets elimination remains strong, the Crows won three fewer games this season and finished five spots lower on the ladder, and their record against the very best in 2026 is hardly inspiring, 2-5 against the top five, including a 52-point thumping at the hands of Saturday's opponent at the same venue. Victory this time would absolutely shore up Nicks' credentials. Another bad loss? The question marks will intensify.

Brisbane's key defenders
Saturday was a horror show for the whole Brisbane line-up, but no-one more than its defenders, and its talls in Harris Andrews, Darcy Gardiner and Ryan Lester specifically, with Sydney pair Charlie Curnow and Logan McDonald booting 11 goals between them. McDonald successfully curbed Andrews' intercepting ability and cashed in with half-a-dozen goals, and Curnow smashed Gardiner. And the equation doesn't get any easier this week with Adelaide's three-pronged tall forward set-up featuring Riley Thilthorpe, Taylor Walker and Darcy Fogarty, who StatMate tells us has kicked at least two goals in his last eight games. Ty Gallop surely is a good chance of returning at Gardiner's expense, or even second ruck Darcy Fort. But whatever selection strings coach Chris Fagan pulls, the Lions can't afford their key backs to be anywhere near that bad again.

You can read more of Rohan Connolly's work at FOOTYOLOGY.

stories.headline: Pochettino cautious about young stars for USMNT camp amid buzz around Sullivan, Hall
stories.summary: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino said that while he is happy about the potential of young players in the U.S. pool, "we need to be careful" amid the buzz around Philadelphia Union's Cavan Sullivan and NYRB's Julian Hall.
stories.body:
United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino said that while he is happy about the potential of young players in the U.S. pool, "we need to be careful" amid the buzz around Philadelphia Union's Cavan Sullivan and Red Bull New York's Julian Hall.

The U.S. has scheduled a quartet of friendlies starting at the end of the month, starting with a match against Peru on Sept. 26, Chile on Sept. 29, Mexico on Oct. 3, and then Canada on Oct. 6. The roster will be announced on Sept. 17, with players beginning to arrive in Atlanta three days later.

As such there is much anticipation about what young players might get called up, including Sullivan and Hall.

Upon signing on for another World Cup cycle last month, Pochettino said he would be "starting from zero" in terms of building his team.

Speaking to reporters via video conference from London, Pochettino stressed he is trying to look at the potential of young players in a balanced way, and not let expectations get ahead of a player's development.

"I think we are very happy about to have all these potential good players being young, and with a possibility to perform and to play," Pochettino said.

"Only we need to be careful. We need to be careful because when you are young, of course you need to be confident, you need to have the trust in yourself, and believe that you can perform and you can do well. But the thing is it's a limit. The balance is the most important.

"And one of our responsibilities is to protect this guy because sometime if you play well and you are 17, 16 or 18 and you play well and people started to know to talk about that you are Messi or you are a big star in the world because you do some few good things. If after you are confused and you don't manage well, that can be dangerous for your career.

"And that is what we don't want. [We want] the young guys with potential being top players to provide the platform for them to evolve and to be professional, to build their career in the best way, improving every day, being humble, being careful when they talk in the media, when they talk with the teammate, when they talk with the opponent. I think respect is the most important thing and they need to be respectful. And of course we want players with talent."

Pochettino said that one goal for this cycle to further eradicate some bad habits that currently exist in the program.

Part of this the alignment of youth and professional clubs with the U.S. Soccer Federation.

The USSF recently announced a takeover of U.S. Youth Soccer.

"I think it's important when we talk about habits, it's about talking about everything, because after the player behave on the field because of this type of decision, they came from the top, he said.

"And we need to be aligned all together in our principles and all the concept that we need to improve if we want to be competitive in every single moment in our [path] until to the first team. I think we are all focused in trying to add our knowledge."

But Pochettino added that the bad habits also include players deciding not to take part competitive tournaments like the Gold Cup.

This a reference to players like Christian Pulisic who opted to sit out the 2025 Gold Cup in order to recover from a long club season.

"We were talking [about] the habit. Before it was difficult to make the roster for the World Cup one year before, because the mindset was different and say, 'Oh, if I play, I have not holidays, I cannot arrive fresh for the World Cup," Pochettino said.

"Already, with the time, you know now that is bulls--- -- sorry -- and I think it's to change this type of idea that are not right and that our experience to build mindset with the coaches, with the people in the organization, in the clubs, and of course us, and then the player that in the way that we will plan and we will do the things is the best for them, for the player, and it's going to be the best for soccer in the USA."

Pochettino added that despite the USMNT playing four games during the window, he will bring in his standard number of 26 players, including four goalkeepers.

Anything more than that would mean some players wouldn't get minutes.

"In this period of the season, we need to be careful with the player that we are going to call," he said.

"We need the players that we'll call that [they] be available to train, but also to play. And I think we consider it at the moment ,and to call 26 players with four keepers. And I think more than this is I think it's an issue because after to train, to share the minutes, I think the player that we are going to have, we want to see, we want to give the possibility to play ... with the possibility to compete. That is the idea for the next camp."

Pochettino indicated that some players who have just switched clubs, like the Middlesbrough duo of defender Max Arfsten and midfielder Sebastian Berhalter, might not be called in in order to give them more time to settle into their new surroundings.

But he indicated there would be a balance between youth and experience.

"I think we cannot bring the whole squad [with] young players because they need to have some guys with experience already competing," Pochettino said.

"But yes, we are going to do a mix ... I think experienced player with young player that can fit together and start to work on how the young kid start to manage the pressure to play in the first team."

stories.headline: Sharks premiership window nowhere near closing: Hynes
stories.summary: Cronulla halfback Nicho Hynes has refuted the widely held claim the Sharks' premiership window is about to close, as the club suffers from finals wobbles and prepares to farewell some big-name stars at season's end.
stories.body:
Cronulla halfback Nicho Hynes has refuted the widely held claim the Sharks' premiership window is about to close, as the club suffers from finals wobbles and prepares to farewell some big-name stars at season's end.

Since Hynes arrived at the Sharks from Storm in 2022, the club has played finals four years in a row but won only three of nine games, although they did the reach the preliminary final the last two seasons.

But at the end of 2026 they will bid goodbye to representative players Siona Katoa and centre Jesse Ramien (Cowboys), Siosifa Talakai (Perth Bears), Cameron McInnes (Super League) and Mawene Hiroti (Titans).

Balancing all that is crafty five-eighth Braydon Trindall, who returns early from a dislocated right shoulder for Saturday night's elimination final against North Queensland, has just turned 27, while rising stars like forwards Tom Hazelton, Jesse Colquhoun and damaging centre KL Iro have only played 60-odd NRL games.

"Whenever we're in this room preparing with the players we have at this club ... I'd be doing an injustice to this club and the players coming through if I said this was our only premiership window," Hynes said.

"It wouldn't be right by the younger players as that would be saying we didn't have belief in them.

"Whoever comes into this facility with a Sharks shirt on or a jersey is always going to do a great job because we've got the coaches and senior players here that make sure that standards are held.

"We've just got a good opportunity (this year) to try and win a premiership and hopefully we'll be doing that for many years to come."

First up is the Cowboys on Saturday night at Allianz Stadium with Trindall, whose nickname is 'Tricky', back in the No.6 jersey after three weeks out.

"Very keen ... it's been very tough sitting on the sidelines so very excited to be back."

Trindall spoke to the media with his shoulder heavily strapped and not knowing yet if postseason surgery is required.

"I just had to get the strength back to where it was, or near-abouts, before I did it," Trindall said.

"I've been working hard to get the mobility through it as well and it feels like it's 100%."

He knows the Cowboys forward pack headed by Jason Taumalolo, Griffin Neame, Heilum Luki and Reuben Cotter will be heading straight for the joint.

"Yep, I'm ready."

Hynes is also ready to reignite the halves partnership that was sporadic in 2022-24, but has been a regular feature for the Sharks the last two years.

"He brings more of a '7' role to the team if you will," Hynes said.

"I know I wear the No.7 -- we can both play that sort of role, but he's got an outstanding kicking game and can play on-ball a bit more which frees me up out the back to play my natural running game.

"That was our first run together out there today and it felt we were back on the bike again.

"When we're chiming in together on both sides of the field it just feels natural."

With a mediocre finals record of late, Hynes was asked which version of the Sharks needed to show up on Saturday.

"Just the best version, and all of you have seen some of the best version of the Sharks this year.

"If we bring that best version of the Sharks we're going to be hard to stop."

stories.headline: Ryan Giggs: Attempted to sway Elliot Anderson to Man United in chance holiday meeting
stories.summary: Ryan Giggs has said that he tried to pitch Manchester United to Elliot Anderson over the summer -- being before asked to "leave me alone."
stories.body:
Manchester United legend Ryan Giggs has said he tried to pitch his former club to Elliot Anderson during a summer holiday -- before being asked to leave the midfielder alone.

The midfielder impressed at Nottingham Forest last season in the Premier League and earned a core role in Thomas Tuchel's England World Cup side, who finished third.

He then completed a move worth up to £116 million ($154m) to United's local rivals Manchester City.

Speaking on the Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast, Giggs said his chance to try and convince Anderson to head to United came when the two crossed paths playing golf in Portugal.

"It was literally a few days before he went to the World Cup. I peppered him," Giggs said.

"He didn't know how to take it at first, and then he relaxed a little bit."

While Anderson may have initially been cordial enough, his demeanour changed after the first few greens.

"But for the first four or five holes, we were literally crossing. And at the end of it, he went, 'will you just let me, leave me alone,'" Giggs said of the interaction.

"Will you just let me play my golf, please? You're in trouble."

Anderson opted for the blue half of Manchester in August, becoming a part of the club's midfield overhaul under Enzo Maresca.

- Marcus Rashford returns to training ahead of Manchester United's Champions League clash

- Another game, more dropped points: Are Man United still a work in progress?

New at the club with him are Enzo Fernández, who commanded a £125m transfer fee from Chelsea, and Ayyoub Bouaddi, the 18-year-old who moved for £81m from Lille.

United, meanwhile moved to secure the acquisitions of Andrey Santos (£50m) from Chelsea, Youri Tielemans (£35m) from Aston Villa and Carlos Baleba (£70m) from Brighton.

Ferdinand, who won his six Premier League titles at United playing with Giggs, added: "You've got to try all sorts to get these deals over. It's mad, though."

"Obviously, the price tag was crazy. And it's just like astronomical money. And Man United ain't got the budget to pay for that."

stories.headline: NBA preview 2026-27: Zach Kram tiers all 30 teams
stories.summary: Six weeks from NBA opening night, Zach Kram is tiering all 30 teams. Which franchises look like Finals contenders?
stories.body:
The games are still weeks away and the practices haven't even started, but the 2026-27 NBA season is fast approaching.

Now that nearly all of the league's important offseason transactions have concluded, and now that the season preview machine is revving up its engines, it's time to take a first broad look at the upcoming landscape. It's too early to conduct an exact 1-to-30 ranking, but we can place each team into a larger tier based on its anticipated standing.

Let's start with the first of eight tiers, featuring the three best teams in the league. (Note: Teams are ordered alphabetically within their tiers.)

Jump to a tier:

The championship favorites

The flawed West contenders

Win machines | High upside

The Southeast Goldilocks tier

Potential play-in participants

Not competitive: Div. A | Div. B

Championship favorites
New York Knicks

Oklahoma City Thunder

San Antonio Spurs

This trio proved to be the top tier of teams last season, and the Knicks, Thunder and Spurs were the only ones to win a game in the conference finals. And they're still in a tier unto themselves. The group will collectively return 14 of the 15 starters in 2026-27, with All-Defensive wing Luguentz Dort (traded from OKC to Atlanta) the only exception.

All three teams enter the new season with championship expectations, and all three are eminently capable of achieving that goal. The Knicks and Thunder are the two most recent winners, and the Spurs reached the Finals much earlier than expected in June, before adding a solid veteran in Tobias Harris over the summer.

Flawed West contenders

Denver Nuggets

Houston Rockets

Los Angeles Lakers

Minnesota Timberwolves

These four teams finished in the 3-to-6 spots in the Western Conference last season, and they're projected to repeat that feat this campaign. Each franchise, however, took a different approach to the offseason.

The Lakers and Timberwolves largely remade their rosters around a couple of stars. The Lakers imported a handful of free agents, led by center Walker Kessler, while the Wolves traded for LaMelo Ball and signed Jonathan Kuminga. But losing LeBron James and the Julius Randle/Naz Reid combo, respectively, could strain both teams' forward rotations, making their offseason transactions high-risk, high-reward endeavors.

Conversely, the Nuggets and Rockets mostly stood pat, with their only roster changes coming to the bench, most notably Denver's loss of Peyton Watson; although Houston would argue the return of Fred VanVleet, who missed all of last season, is the biggest upgrade. The Rockets also extended forward Amen Thompson to a five-year deal last week, ensuring his future with the team's young core of Alperen Sengun, Jabari Smith Jr. and Tari Eason.

Regular-season win machines
Boston Celtics

Cleveland Cavaliers

Detroit Pistons

Boston, Cleveland and Detroit represented three of the top four Eastern Conference teams in the 2025-26 regular season, and all three should remain in the 50-plus-win range despite the conference's boost in overall depth. The Celtics had the biggest personnel loss of the group with the Jaylen Brown trade, but they also should benefit from a full season of Jayson Tatum, after he played only 16 games last season.

The bigger question for this threesome, however, is how much postseason upside there is, even if each team lands another high playoff seed. The Celtics seemed to lose some championship equity when they traded their recent Finals MVP, coming off the best season of his career.

After taking the East's No. 1 seed last season, the Pistons didn't address their greatest weakness this summer, as they still lack secondary scoring behind Cade Cunningham. And as of this writing, All-NBA center Jalen Duren remains unsigned in restricted free agency.

And finally, while the Cavaliers took a big, necessary swing by trading a bunch of depth (and an unprotected first-round pick) for Peyton Watson, it's still unclear whether a backcourt built around two extremely offense-first guards in Donovan Mitchell and James Harden can hold up in the playoff pressure cooker. The Cavs took a step forward by making the East finals, before getting swept by the Knicks. Watson hasn't proved himself in a postseason setting, either, after missing the 2025-26 playoffs due to injury.

High-upside Finals contenders
Indiana Pacers

Miami Heat

Philadelphia 76ers

Toronto Raptors

It's unclear whether any of these teams, all of which won 46 games or fewer last season, will break into the top four in the East standings. But they still have significant playoff upside because there is so much combined star power: Tyrese Haliburton, Pascal Siakam, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, Joel Embiid, Kawhi Leonard (presumably) and Scottie Barnes.

There's a reasonable argument for each team to reach the Finals, as long as one important what if goes the right way. The Pacers could return to the Finals if Haliburton plays like his former self in his return from an Achilles tendon tear. The Heat could reach the Finals if Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr. provide enough shooting and supplemental offense around the frontcourt stars. The 76ers could reach the Finals if the stars mesh and Embiid is fresh in April and May. And the Raptors could reach the Finals if Leonard, Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles lead the conference's best defense.

Solid Southeast squads

Atlanta Hawks

Orlando Magic

These Southeast Division rivals occupy their own sort of Goldilocks tier: Their ceiling is too low to fit in any of the earlier groups, but their floor is too high to go any later.

Their similarities extend further than that:

They finished in close proximity to each other last season, as Atlanta won 46 games and Orlando won 45, and both threatened to pull off a playoff upset before fading. And both made meaningful offseason upgrades, as the Hawks traded for Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins, while the Magic hired new coach Sean Sweeney in an attempt to turn all of their potential into better production.

Potential play-in participants
Charlotte Hornets

Dallas Mavericks

Golden State Warriors

Memphis Grizzlies

New Orleans Pelicans

Phoenix Suns

Portland Trail Blazers

Utah Jazz

Washington Wizards

The largest tier features teams that could conceivably finish near the bottom of the standings but also could sneak into the playoffs.

In the East, Charlotte could take a step back this season after its scorching finish to the 2025-26 campaign. Trading LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges might have been the best move for the franchise's ultimate long-term plans, but Ball, in particular, was integral to the team's run last season. In the crowded East race, it wouldn't be a surprise for the Hornets to finish outside of the top 10.

The Wizards are attempting to crash that party -- and could do so, if Trae Young, Anthony Davis and No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa all mesh and stay healthy. But they have a long way to climb after winning just 15, 18 and 17 games across the past three seasons, and full health from Davis is far from guaranteed.

The largest takeaway from this tier comes out West, though, where the race looks incredibly jumbled after the top six.

Phoenix and Portland both reached the playoffs last season, though neither seems to raise a very high ceiling. New Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori will have to integrate a newly star-studded yet injury-prone backcourt featuring Damian Lillard and Ja Morant. Meanwhile, Golden State didn't make any splashes this offseason and will await Jimmy Butler III's return from a torn ACL.

Elsewhere, the Mavericks and Jazz could surge up the standings thanks to full seasons from Kyrie Irving and Jaren Jackson Jr., respectively, as well as further development from Dallas' Cooper Flagg and Utah's young guards. New Orleans won only 26 games last season and didn't do much beyond adding Bennedict Mathurin this summer, but there is still plenty of talent -- Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy III, Dejounte Murray, Herbert Jones -- on its roster.

Finally, don't sleep on Memphis, with its sneaky upside. Ty Jerome and Zach Edey were excellent in limited playing time last season, and No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer could provide instant impact, even as a rookie. If all three players stay healthy, the Grizzlies could approach a .500 record.

Noncompetitive, with their own pick
Chicago Bulls

Sacramento Kings

The final two tiers occupy the same broad space in the standings, as the five teams within them are unlikely to contend this season. But one key difference separates Chicago and Sacramento from the final trio: The Bulls and Kings possess their own 2027 first-rounder, which means they're incentivized to win enough games to maximize their lottery odds, due to the new rules that penalize the teams with the three worst records in the league.

The Bulls should be good enough to avoid that fate, after adding veterans Norman Powell and Nic Claxton in the offseason; although Chicago's primary goal should be developing the young frontcourt duo of Matas Buzelis and rookie Caleb Wilson.

Meanwhile, Sacramento hopes a full season of Domantas Sabonis, Zach LaVine and Keegan Murray -- after the trio combined to play just 81 games last season -- will boost its win total out of the so-called relegation zone, though the Kings' eyes are set on a future led by rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr.

Noncompetitive, without their own pick
Brooklyn Nets

LA Clippers

Milwaukee Bucks

Unlike the Bulls and Kings, these final three teams won't even reap the rewards of their own subpar record next spring: The Nets owe a pick swap to Houston, the Clippers owe a pick swap to Oklahoma City and the Bucks owe their first-rounder outright to either Atlanta or New Orleans.

Counterintuitively, those deals could make tanking more likely from this trio, because they shouldn't care if their traded picks' lottery odds are depressed. Still, there's enough talent here to make 60-plus losses fairly unlikely.

Brooklyn added Julius Randle while retaining Michael Porter Jr. The Clippers have two recent All-Stars in Darius Garland and Brandon Ingram (assuming the Kawhi Leonard deal goes through). The Bucks lost Giannis Antetokounmpo, of course, but they now have a half dozen quality guards on their roster, including former All-Star Tyler Herro in a contract year.

stories.headline: Kimi Raikkonen's son Robin, 11, joins Red Bull junior team
stories.summary: Robin Raikkonen, the 11-year-old son of 2007 Formula 1 world champion Kimi, has joined Red Bull Racing's driver development programme.
stories.body:
Robin Raikkonen, the 11-year-old son of 2007 Formula 1 world champion Kimi, has joined Red Bull Racing's driver development programme.

Robin is currently racing in go-karts -- the first step towards single seater race cars -- and has already achieved success in national and international Rotax and WSK championships.

The Raikkonen family has shared regular posts of his progress through karting via Instagram, from his very early days in junior go-karts to his participation in championship events.

"Robin has already demonstrated exceptional ability in karting," Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said.

"His speed, racecraft and natural talent have established him as one of the most promising young drivers in his age group. At the same time, he impresses with his maturity, his calm approach and his clear focus on driving.

"Our goal is to develop him step by step, without placing any unnecessary pressure on his shoulders. The path through motorsport is a long one, and we will give him the time, support and resources he needs to maximise his potential.

"We strongly believe that talent can thrive when supported by the right people, the right culture and the right environment. That is what we are committed to providing Robin as he continues his development. We are very much looking forward to taking the next steps in his journey together with Robin and his family."

Red Bull's young driver programme has been one of the most successful in the paddock, paving the way for four-time world champions Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen to enter the sport.

The team recently announced that it had signed Mercedes' talent scout Gwen Lagrue to head up the programme from the start of next year, which is also when Raikkonen will join.

- Alpine's Pierre Gasly sums up rollercoaster Italian GP: 'Story of my life'

The programme benefits from having two teams on the grid in Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls, allowing drivers to make their F1 debut with the junior team before stepping up to the senior team.

"We are all thrilled and excited that Robin has been chosen to further his racing path as a member of the Red Bull Junior Team," Kimi Raikkonen said. "Laurent and everyone else at Red Bull have been incredibly supportive throughout all our discussions.

"They offer a compelling and comprehensive programme to develop and nurture Robin's progress over the coming years and provide him with all the experience required to develop his natural talent, which has amply been displayed in all his karting endeavours to date.

"Red Bull's Junior Team has had years of incredible success. Its alumni include Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen amongst many others. It is thus with great humility that Robin joins this illustrious programme, and he will dedicate all his efforts to warrant the trust that Red Bull is placing in him."

Aside from the drivers currently racing for Red Bull's two teams on the grid, Carlos Sainz, Alex Albon and Pierre Gasly all arrived in F1 through Red Bull's junior programme.

stories.headline: How to draft, play and win your fantasy hockey league like an expert
stories.summary: It's not just who you draft, it's everything that happens after. An expert guide to play fantasy hockey like the pros.
stories.body:
Let's go! Coming off a long summer following one of the most exciting hockey seasons ever, on and off the NHL ice, we're ready to re-embrace the game we love, as both fans and invested fantasy managers. Whether you're a wily veteran or brand new to the game, we're here to help you not only compete but give yourself a solid shot at victory. Starting with this primer that serves as an introduction for newbies and a refresher for those more well-versed.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

The draft

The most important two hours of your entire fantasy hockey season. But don't sweat it! A little research and preparation is all it takes to cobble together a competitive roster. To start, don't overcomplicate matters, take the best player available. This year, that's Nathan MacKinnon, Nikita Kucherov, Macklin Celebrini, or Connor McDavid (yes, even under new defensive-minded head coach Mike Babcock).

Once that elite quartet is off the board, turn to the second tier of elite forwards including Leon Draisaitl, Jason Robertson, and David Pastrnak. Your blue line and net can wait a moment. Cale Makar isn't fetching you fantasy points for dollars earned and there are enough good-to-great goalies even once Andrei Vasilevskiy is off the table. Grab your big scorer up front, first and foremost. These are the skaters who can average 3.0-plus per game in ESPN standard points leagues.

Use the next few early rounds to acquire at least one premiere fantasy defenseman and a top-tier netminder (more on those positions below), while always keeping an eye out for the remaining gems up front. Don't fret about filling positional requirements at this stage and continue to grab the heavy hitters. I promise the fantasy math will eventually work out in your favor.

Okay, once the best players are off the board, and your top-tier goalie is secured, now start working to satisfy positional and categorical needs. Too many right-wingers will result in too many quality performers stuck on your bench on busier nights. While a dearth at another position is also frustratingly limiting. Of course, if your league adheres to the overarching (F) classification, continue to draft the best player available. In later rounds, it's time to really focus on sleepers, bounce-back and breakout contenders. These potential pleasant surprises can truly alter a roster for the better.

Back to the importance of research and preparation, as usual, we're here to help with preseason previews covering all matters fantasy hockey right up until your draft and beyond.

ESPN Fantasy Hockey is the fun, free way to get inside the game. Draft your players, set your lineups and earn points when the pros do. Sign up today!

Bounce-back and breakout candidates

With the top center in San Jose serving as the poster child for breakout candidates in 2025-26, Celebrini wasn't alone in taking a leap forward. The Anaheim Ducks' Cutter Gauthier impressed us with his 41-goal statement season just as (then) Tampa Bay Lightning defender Darren Raddysh won over alert managers by finishing 11th in fantasy points, despite missing nine games. Cole Caufield followed linemate Nick Suzuki's lead from the previous season by exploding for 88 points, including 51 goals. Will linemate Juraj Slafkovsky be next in busting through the 80-point mark? Meanwhile in Philadelphia, Dan Vladar proved he does indeed have the chops to serve as a No. 1 netminder. Easier said than done, but spotting these characters before they erupt can go a long way to ameliorating your fantasy squad.

Zach Benson of the Buffalo Sabres could be one such candidate, after making such a positive impression this past spring. Poised to see top-line minutes alongside Tage Thompson, the scrappy winger feels on the verge of going next-level. Celebrini's roommate, Will Smith is also in ideal position to erupt at age 21. On the blue line, I like Cole Hutson of the Washington Capitals to wow us as a rookie, and Jet Greaves is in position to finally establish himself as a prominent fantasy netminder for the Columbus Blue Jackets.

As for bounce-back performers, goalie Jeremy Swayman and forward Ryan O'Reilly are just two examples of figures who rebounded off rather drab campaigns the previous year. Now I have my sights set on Tampa Bay's Brayden Point and Capitals newbie Jordan Kyrou to do the same. Elias Pettersson is an intriguing figure -- altogether not a bad fantasy performer despite his disappointing play in Vancouver -- as someone who might finally get back to the player he was under new management and a fresh coaching staff. The former 100-point forward very much might be worth a roll of the fantasy dice.

Less appealing "B" candidates

Backsliders. Maybe they're coming off a season that's just too anomalous and tough to duplicate. Age could be another factor, along with a new role within the lineup or on another team altogether. Whatever the reason, these players are moving in the wrong direction production-wise, and you want to avoid them.

Boston's Morgan Geekie potted 25 goals in his first 36 games and then just another 14 in the following 45 contests. Managers unfamiliar with that timing and trend might be unjustifiably wooed by the total of 39 and mistake the winger for a 40-goal scorer. When in reality, even if he remains on a top line with Pastrnak, the 28-year-old sports true 30-goal potential at heart.

Does Alex DeBrincat score another 40-plus with Patrick Kane back in Chicago? Considering that loss and the state of hockey with the Detroit Red Wings at present, I wouldn't predict as much. Sure, ex-Sabre Alex Tuch could flirt with the 35-goal and 70-point mark once more on a line with Dylan Strome and Alex Ovechkin in Washington, or enjoy more modest numbers on another unit. Just as some players are going to improve statistically with a different supporting cast, others will move in the opposite direction, and expectations should be tempered.

This isn't to suggest you shouldn't draft Geekie, DeBrincat, Tuch and others, just don't jump on them too early with the mind you're getting last year's exact fantasy model.

More on goalies

You won't win your league, or even make a go of it, with bad fantasy goaltending. Snoozing on this position is not an option. These few competitors are responsible for far too many categories. So as tempting as it may be to snag another high-performing skater when it's the right time to address your needs in net, take the latter route.

The first rule of thumb is to avoid netminders on lousy teams. Arguably the best goaltender in the world played 57 games for a surprisingly bad squad in Winnipeg this past season. By the time mid-April rolled around, Connor Hellebuyck netted his managers fewer fantasy points than 27 others in the league. Taking large personal strides, Spencer Knight served as a promising figure for the Blackhawks through yet another rebuilding campaign in Chicago. Yet despite making 22 more starts than Jesper Wallstedt in Minnesota, Knight still finished well below the Wild netminder in the fantasy standings. No matter how individually talented, great goalies on an inferior teams most often aren't in position to regularly reward their managers.

But busy is good too. Once zoned in on the better teams in the league, it's wise to target those who play the most. Tampa Bay's Vasilevskiy is a great example, as is Dallas Stars netminder Jake Oettinger. Logan Thompson presents as a top-five fantasy netminder, again, on a Capitals team that should be even better. While the league continues to trend in the direction of relying on two or more figures between the pipes, there's still a good number of goalies who carry a significantly heavier workload. Such characters on quality squads need to be chased, first and foremost.

After your top performers are secured, give prominent starters on improving teams and top-tier tandem members a look. It's Greaves' net in Columbus. If the Blue Jackets can equal or improve-upon their record from this past run, the 25-year-old will prove valuable. As for old faces in new places, ex-New Jersey Devils netminder Jacob Markstrom could be in for nice rebound campaign with the Florida Panthers.

Colorado's Scott Wedgewood reigns supreme as member of the tandem crowd, while Stanley Cup Champ Brandon Bussi should see more starts than Pyotr Kotchetkov now that Frederik Andersen is in Edmonton. The options open up considerably, again, once your recognized heavy-hitters are in place.

For more on how to address this all-important position, check out our dedicated goalie preview.

A slightly deeper dive on D-men

Unlike in years past, Makar is no longer a list of one as far as premier fantasy defenders are concerned. Six blueliners -- Makar, Zach Werenski, Evan Bouchard, Moritz Seider, Charlie McAvoy and Jake Sanderson -- all averaged between 2.4 and 2.6 fantasy points/game in ESPN standard leagues this past season. While Makar and Bouchard sit a titch above the rest, the gap is much smaller than before. Another good throng, including Quinn Hughes, Rasmus Dahlin and Lane Hutson, banged out 2.2 points/game in 2025-26. In most leagues, you want at least one top-tier performer, along with a pair from that secondary, yet still impressive, sub-set. Then take a breath.

In competition that rewards blocked-shots, there's no real sense of urgency in padding your fantasy roster with defenders. This past campaign, 29 blueliners earned between 1.7 and 2.1 fantasy points/game. Plenty to go around. Instead, pursue skaters that are going to put up the flashiest numbers first, regardless of position. Of course, as with every position, when rounding out your defensive corps, keep an eye out for prospective breakout candidates. The Los Angeles Kings' Brandt Clarke and Capitals rookie Cole Hutson are two such names on my 2026-27 radar.

Leagues, leagues, leagues

As for customization, ESPN Fantasy provides the forum to create any type of league you want. If interested in constructing your own head-to-head competition, first settle on either the points or categories path, then determine the applicable stats. Beyond scoring, hits and blocked-shots -- to reward defensive play -- are more popular than ever. Maybe you're a faceoff enthusiast, and want to compensate the best and busiest in the dot. Have a penchant for penalty minutes? PIM remains an option, along with a good variety of others to suit your fantasy hockey tastes. Managers who don't care to customize can always opt for our default head-to-head points league, referenced above, which remains widely popular.

For those who want to kick it old school, Rotisserie (Roto) competition awards points based on where your players rank as a collective in every category. For instance, in a 12-team league, the group of skaters that boasts the most total goals, at any given time, retain the maximum 12 points. The fantasy team with the worst plus/minus receives just one. And so on, cumulatively and fluidly, through each category to arrive at a combined sum. H2H category leagues differ from points leagues in that not only one goal, but one hit or one blocked-shot, can mean the difference between victory and defeat regarding that particular stat. Scores carry forward and add up throughout the campaign -- say, 6-4, then 3-7 etc. -- unlike in a head-to-head points battle where you either win the week or you don't.

Once the parameters and makeup of your league are set, decide how much time you want to invest in adjusting your lineup. Every day, every week, or never again, in honor of how we used to pen-and-paper-it back in the pre-internet days of yore.

Made it this far? Create your own league with your own rules and play against your friends today.

Categories matter

Becoming intimately acquainted with your league's specific categories is essential to success. Not only with the stats themselves, but how much weight they carry. One hit in category leagues makes a greater impact than when only worth 0.1 points otherwise. If assists are equivalent to goals, Lane Hutson is nearly equal to Makar as a fantasy performer. Conversely, a sniper like Steven Stamkos (at least in his second season with the Nashville Predators) boasts a lot more shine in fantasy competition where goals double helpers in value. If blocked-shots don't count, a defender like Toronto's Jake McCabe belongs nowhere near your fantasy roster. Anyway, you get the idea.

Investing in mock drafts

The more you mock draft, the better. While practice doesn't necessarily make perfect in this case, it certainly helps. These dress rehearsals will offer you insight as to how other managers are navigating the draft along with player preferences. If everyone is avoiding a high-ranked skater there's likely a reason why. You'll also be better prepared for certain trends -- a too-early run on goalies, for instance -- after experiencing one for pretend. Plus, they're fun. Check out our Mock Draft Lobby, pick the room that best represents your own fantasy league, and take a spin.

Not sure how to play? Try out the ESPN Mock Draft Lobby.

Building a dynasty

This style of fantasy competition suits those who want to play the long game. Most akin to the real-life NHL affair, managing a dynasty hockey squad requires patience and foresight. Barring trades, you're stuck with these players, like it or not, for the haul. Last season, I recommended grabbing Matthew Schaefer right off the top, even if he didn't end up playing in the NHL full-time (a laughable concept now). This year, that's Leafs No. 1 pick Gavin McKenna, who is expected to suit up right away. Our fantasy rookie rundown will further help with who to target for what's likely to be a long, and hopefully happy, dynasty fantasy marriage.

Keeper leagues are different in that you're able to jettison your lesser players each season and keep only those most treasured. How to approach the draft in rounding out your roster largely depends on your club's current state. Are you rich with peak talent and ready to win now? Then go on and grab some aging veterans to help with that championship push. Otherwise, if your team is still also in the building phase, similar to many real NHL clubs, it's wiser to invest in younger, gifted players who sport the wherewithal to be great down the road.

Roster maintenance

This is the fun part. Outside of set-and-forget leagues, how well you fiddle with your roster will determine whether you're still in the championship hunt once spring rolls around, or already looking ahead to next season. Striking the right balance is of ultimate importance, as too much tinkering -- for instance losing patience with an underperforming player and prematurely letting them go -- can also bite you in the behind.

Even before puck-drop on day one, it's essential to become familiar with your pool of available free agents. I guarantee a few will emerge as valuable fantasy performers in those first few weeks, or even days. Whether their success is due to an unexpected line assignment or another factor. Trust me, these players will already be rostered by the most vigilant managers before others even realize what's going on. To repeat, the first few weeks of the season are absolutely integral in allowing you the chance to improve your roster, by swapping in unanticipated performers for your lesser draft choices.

With so few candidates available, goalies are especially important to monitor early on. Raise your hand if you had Carolina Hurricanes waiver pickup Brandon Bussi on your fantasy roster to start 2025-26. Right. After going 31-6-2 (2.44 GAA) in the regular season, the 28-year-old Stanley Cup champion is now considered a top-15 fantasy netminder heading into 2026-27. Your responsibility is to identify this season's Bussi and snag him before anyone else.

One last tip on roster maintenance: Set every day's lineup at the start of the week. You can always shift players around later, but at least there's a reasonable lineup in place if you can't address it for a day or two.

A word on injured reserve

Use those IR slots to your advantage, beginning with the draft. You can always move out such inactive players for others, if necessary, once the league is in full swing. For instance, in all but the shallowest of leagues, Seth Jarvis should be accounted for on draft day, even though he's not expected back from shoulder surgery until November or December. The Carolina forward checks too many fantasy boxes, too well, to leave on the board. The boost he'll provide your squad, once back to health, could prove tangibly beneficial once we're into the meat of the season.

Similarly to the real-life game, it's like trading for a quality player mid-season without giving anything up (other than dumping your biggest roster disappointment). The same applies to Chicago's Connor Bedard, Edmonton's Frederik Andersen, and others. Fill up those IR slots with banged-up placeholders in later stages of your draft. If you need to pivot and jettison Jarvis later because Nathan MacKinnon suffers an injury, so be it.

The art of trades

In my decades of covering and playing fantasy hockey, I've noticed that the most active managers are often the most successful. That goes beyond working the wire. Particularly in deeper leagues, trades are a great way to improve your roster when there's an obvious weakness. Such deals are not tools used to scam another manager. Ideally, both partners come away filling a void. Your goalie for their high-performing winger etc. Maybe you need to address one specific categorical box, such as hits or blocked shots. If most of your fellow managers are trade wary, keep at it. You're likely to find a dance partner eventually. Unless this is you, start with those who are stuck with lousy goaltending. They're usually the most desperate.

With that, here's to a fantastic fantasy season in 2026-27. Good luck!

stories.headline: 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup: Team USA and quarterfinal preview
stories.summary: The U.S. women and France remain front-runners as the knockout stage arrives in Berlin, but who else has impressed?
stories.body:
BERLIN -- The quarterfinals are nearly set for the 2026 FIBA World Cup, with 10 teams still in the hunt for a spot on the podium in Germany this weekend.

The United States, France and Belgium are the only countries still undefeated, though Italy tested the U.S. women in their second group game. The Americans eked out a 55-52 victory, their lowest-scoring World Cup performance since 1971.

Those three teams, along with Spain (2-1), punched their tickets to Thursday's quarterfinals. On Tuesday, Hungary beat Japan and Germany topped Korea to also secure spots in the final eight. The next pair of berths will go to the winners of Wednesday's qualification showdowns between China-Puerto Rico and Australia-Italy.

Here's what you need to know about how the United States has performed and how the rest of the field ranks as we turn the page to the knockout rounds.

Jump to:

AUS | BEL | CHN | FRA | GER

HUN | ITA | PUR | ESP | USA

Power Rankings | Team USA analysis

In what areas has Team USA been most impressive?
As is the case with other U.S. women's teams, the depth of talent continues to stand out. Coach Kara Lawson has started the five returning senior team players -- Napheesa Collier, Kahleah Copper, Chelsea Gray, Breanna Stewart and Jackie Young -- each game this tournament, meaning the likes of Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers, Aliyah Boston and Angel Reese are coming off the bench -- an enviable position to every other country in this event.

Watching the United States at its best -- as ESPN colleague Michael Voepel put it during the 94-61 win over China -- is like watching a movie in which every role is played by an Oscar winner. And if the U.S. women are getting stops, getting out in transition, sharing the ball and making the opponent pay on the other end, it's world-class basketball.

For the most part, each player on the roster has had some strong moments so far this tournament -- even after the vets struggled mightily most of the Italy game, they were the ones who made winning plays down the stretch to ensure the United States remained undefeated. The Young and Turnt crew don't always get everything perfect, but they have shown they belong. Having so many newcomers will pay dividends in the future in terms of experience, but Team USA will need them now to ensure the team goes home with a fifth consecutive World Cup gold medal.

Where have the Americans struggled?
The U.S. women aren't immune from defensive breakdowns, which isn't shocking given the team came together so last minute and chemistry is developing in real time. But the biggest concern is how the USA will generate offense when things don't come easily.

It's unlikely the U.S. women will score 55 points and shoot below 30% from the field again this tournament (or maybe even this decade) as they did against Italy. But the performance was eerily reminiscent of the France game from the 2024 Olympics, another close call but with a gold medal on the line.

The U.S. women's efficiency in this tournament has been much lower than we're used to seeing: 43.4%, ranking eighth, and a 29% accuracy from the 3-point arc (11th in the field) -- all while not generating a ton of looks from deep (23 per game).

This is where not having A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum -- two players very capable of going to get a bucket -- really hurts. Which players, or what combinations, will create offense if things become stagnant?

During TNT's FIBA World Cup studio show, three-time U.S. Olympic gold medalist Tina Charles said after the Italy game that she didn't see anyone pull Team USA together and essentially say, "Enough, get it together, let's end this now." With no Diana Taurasi or Wilson around, that's Stewart's or Gray's role moving forward, with their play on the court and in how they lead their teammates.

World Cup Power Rankings

1. United States (3-0)
Current WNBA players:

F/C Aliyah Boston, Indiana Fever

G Paige Bueckers, Dallas Wings

G Sonia Citron, Washington Mystics

G Caitlin Clark, Indiana Fever

F Napheesa Collier, Minnesota Lynx

F/G Kahleah Copper, Phoenix Mercury

G Chelsea Gray, Las Vegas Aces

G Rhyne Howard, Atlanta Dream

F Kiki Iriafen, Washington Mystics

F Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream

F Breanna Stewart, New York Liberty

G Jackie Young, Las Vegas Aces

Pre-tournament rank: 1

Next opponent: Quarterfinals vs. Hungary (5:30 a.m. ET Thursday)

How they've looked: The U.S. women are right where everyone expected them to be: undefeated and playing in the quarterfinals. But their path so far hasn't been without some struggles. Though two of the United States' group games -- victories over China and Czechia by 30-plus points each -- reflected the dominance we've come to expect, the 55-52 win against Italy neared catastrophe. It was Team USA's smallest margin of victory in the World Cup since 1979 and its first World Cup game decided by single digits since 2010.

The U.S. women rebounded by scoring more first-half points against Czechia (57) than they totaled against Italy, and they hope to bring that momentum into the knockout rounds. Eight players are averaging at least six points, and no one is averaging more than 12 (Young is the team leader with 11.3 PPG).

2. France (3-0)
Current WNBA players:

G Pauline Astier, New York Liberty

F Valeriane Ayayi, Phoenix Mercury

G Marine Johannes, New York Liberty

G Leila Lacan, Connecticut Sun

G Carla Leite, Portland Fire

C Dominique Malonga, Seattle Storm

F Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries

G Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries

Other notable players: C Marieme Badiane

Pre-tournament rank: 2

Next opponent: Quarterfinals vs. Wednesday's China-Puerto Rico winner (8:30 a.m. ET Thursday)

How they've looked: France was considered the top challenger to U.S. entering the World Cup and still appears to be the biggest contender. In fact, the French have a strong argument to top this ranking, having outscored opponents by a tournament-best 127 points. Their defense gave the U.S. women fits at the Paris Olympics, but so far in Berlin, Les Bleues have scored at least 95 points each game, with dynamic duo Williams (the tournament's leading scorer with 18.7 PPG) and Johannes combining for 36 PPG.

3. Belgium (3-0)
Current WNBA players:

G Julie Allemand, Toronto Tempo

C Kyara Linskens, Phoenix Mercury

F Antonia Delaere, Minnesota Lynx

Other notable players: F Emma Meesseman, G Julie Vanloo, F Bethy Mununga

Pre-tournament rank: 4

Next opponent: Quarterfinals vs. Germany (11:45 a.m. ET Thursday)

How they've looked: Belgium predictably came out of Group C unscathed, winning each of its first three games by double figures. And just as expected, Meesseman has been one of the best players in the tournament, averaging 18.3 points, 8.0 rebounds, 5.3 assists and 1.7 blocks. Belgium is the better team on paper, but Germany will be playing with extra pride and a boisterous home crowd behind it in the quarterfinals.

4. Spain (2-1)
Current WNBA players:

G Elena Buenavida, Minnesota Lynx (developmental player)

C Raquel Carrera, New York Liberty

F Maria Conde, Toronto Tempo

C Megan DiLeo, Portland Fire

C Awa Fam, Seattle Storm

G Alicia Florez, Washington Mystics

Other notable players: G Iyana Martin, G Maite Cazorla

Pre-tournament rank: 3

Next opponent: Quarterfinals vs. Wednesday's Italy-Australia winner (2:45 p.m. ET Thursday)

How they've looked: Spain looked poised to be one of the more exciting teams to take the court in Berlin but enters the quarterfinals with a 2-1 record after suffering a stunning loss to Mali in the second game of group play. The Spanish can still get to the podium for their fourth time in as many tournament appearances, but that kind of run would surely necessitate their young duo of Martin (17.3 PPG) and Fam (12.3 PPG) to play beyond their years in big moments.

5. Australia (2-1)
Current WNBA players:

F Chloe Bibby, Minnesota Lynx

G Isobel Borlase, Atlanta Dream

C Ezi Magbegor, Seattle Storm

G Jade Melbourne, Seattle Storm

F Alanna Smith, Dallas Wings

G Miela Sowah, Golden State Valkyries

F Stephanie Talbot, Las Vegas Aces

Other notable players: F Alex Fowler, G Alex Wilson

Pre-tournament rank: 7

Next opponent: vs. Italy (2:45 p.m. ET Wednesday) in a must-win to advance to the quarterfinals

How they've looked: It hasn't been the easiest ride for Sandy Brondello's team. Already missing Sami Whitcomb because of injury before the World Cup, Australia lost Smith 12 minutes into its first game in Berlin. She hasn't played since and her status for the knockout rounds is unknown. After taking care of Puerto Rico and Turkiye, the Australians kept up with Belgium (a 80-68 loss) but now have to go through a gritty Italy squad for a spot in the final eight.

6. China (2-1)
Current WNBA players:

C Han Xu, New York Liberty

Pre-tournament rank: 6

Next opponent: vs. Puerto Rico (11:45 p.m. ET Wednesday) in a must-win to advance to the quarterfinals

How they've looked: The World Cup has been a roller coaster for China. The team was routed by the U.S. in its first game, nearly lost to Czechia the next time out before pulling away in overtime and then put together a convincing 20-point win over Italy to close group play. Assuming China gets past Puerto Rico, France is a tough matchup awaiting in the quarters. Han Xu has been their superstar, averaging 17.3 points, 11.3 rebounds and 2.7 assists.

7. Germany (3-1)
Current WNBA players:

F Frieda Buhner, Portland Fire

G Leonie Fiebich, New York Liberty

C Luisa Geiselsoder, Portland Fire

F Nyara Sabally, Toronto Tempo

Other notable players: F Emily Bessoir, F Lina Sontag, C Marie Gülich and G Alexis Peterson

Pre-tournament rank: 5

Next opponent: Quarterfinals vs. Belgium (11:45 a.m. ET Thursday)

How they've looked: After being trounced by Spain to open the tournament, Germany has won three straight, including Tuesday's clobbering of Korea to clinch a spot in the quarters. A quarterfinal appearance is a good step for a program appearing in only its second World Cup, but Germany is hoping it can capitalize on being a host and having a talented squad. Buhner has had a strong tournament, averaging a team-high 15.3 points.

8. Hungary (3-1)
Current WNBA players:

F Dorka Juhász, Minnesota Lynx

Other notable players: G Yvonne Turner

Pre-tournament rank: 11

Next opponent: Quarterfinals vs. United States (5:30 a.m. ET Thursday)

How they've looked: It has been a memorable World Cup for Hungary, which is appearing in the event for the first time since 1998. The team was throttled by France to start the tournament but hasn't lost since on its way to the quarterfinals. Though Juhász carried Hungary through group play with averages of 17 points and 12.3 rebounds, Reka Lelik was the team's star Tuesday, finishing with a game-high 23 points, eight rebounds and four assists against Japan.

9. Italy (1-2)
Current WNBA players:

G Costanza Verona, Dallas Wings (developmental player)

F Cecilia Zandalasini, Golden State Valkyries

Other notable players: F Lorela Cubaj

Pre-tournament rank: 8

Next opponent: vs. Australia (2:45 p.m. ET Wednesday) in a must-win to advance to the quarterfinals

How they've looked: Before Berlin, Italy hadn't appeared in either the World Cup or Olympics since 1996. But the Italians have already made a name for themselves by nearly taking down the United States behind their physicality, zone defense, passionate play and the efforts of Zandalasini. But Italy suffered a letdown the next day against China and now has the tall task of facing an Opals squad that as a program is much more experienced on the global stage.

10. Puerto Rico (1-2)
Current WNBA players: None

Other notable players: G Arella Guirantes, C Imani McGee-Stafford

Pre-tournament rank: 16

Next opponent: vs. China (11:45 p.m. ET Wednesday) in a must-win to advance to the quarterfinals

How they've looked: Puerto Rico's sole win was by four points over Turkiye, but its losses to Australia and Belgium were both competitive. The team is led by a big three of McGree-Stafford (the top rebounder in the tournament with 13 boards per game), Guirantes and Trinity San Antonio, who combine to average 46.7 points. A win over China would give Puerto Rico consecutive appearances in the World Cup quarterfinals.
